source.title: MedSAE: Dissecting MedCLIP Representations with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Riccardo Renzulli; Colas Lepoutre; E. Cassano; Marco Grangetto

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; full paper text, including appendix, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures feature-label correlations and interpretation accuracy in MedCLIP embeddings and SAE features, rather than using the original studies’ methods for identifying polysemantic neurons.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates monosemanticity in raw MedCLIP embeddings and SAE features, including label-correlation entropy and automated interpretation detection. It does not test the specific InceptionV1 neuron or whether its example inputs share a feature. Figure-based detection distributions are described qualitatively in the text; their exact values are not reported. The composite-image experiment tests embedding linearity, not whether feature superposition causes polysemanticity.
record.test_reason: The study applies ReLU sparse autoencoders to MedCLIP final-layer embeddings and scores its own SAE features against raw embedding dimensions. It assumes superposition and does not test it. It reports no rate of polysemantic neurons in any model. An SAE is a post-hoc decomposition, not a change to the model's activation function, architecture or training, so it does not bear on V5. The raw-embedding baseline is a class-correlation entropy over 14 co-occurring CheXpert labels: 2.38 against a maximum of about 3.81. That measure cannot show neurons responding to unrelated inputs as V1 describes. The composite-image test checks embedding linearity, not capacity pressure (V3).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that ReLU SAEs extract more class-selective, interpretable, approximately monosemantic features than raw MedCLIP embeddings. They also claim, from the composite-image check, that MedCLIP embeddings approximately satisfy linear superposition. They note limits: a single backbone, the ReLU SAE trade-offs and dead units, sensitivity of naming to sample selection, and the need for expert validation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ReLU sparse autoencoders on MedCLIP embeddings and evaluates class-correlation entropy and MedGemma-generated feature names; it does not reproduce the original neuron visualization or SoLU methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported relation between entropy and sparsity–reconstruction trade-off is non-monotonic; neuron naming is described as sensitive to selection of top-activating samples.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features on MedCLIP embeddings have slightly lower label-correlation entropy (2.25 vs 2.38) and more high-accuracy automated interpretations (21 vs 2) than raw embedding dimensions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse autoencoder features are more monosemantic than raw embedding dimensions in medical vision-language models.

fits_no_version.finding: Composite chest X-ray embeddings are reconstructed linearly from their component embeddings with cosine similarity 0.97.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MedCLIP embeddings of composite images approximately follow a linear combination of component embeddings.

record.problems: Only the MedCLIP-ResNet backbone is tested. The authors note 30% dead neurons, sensitivity of automated naming to top-activating sample selection, and the need for medical-expert validation. The detection-accuracy distributions and sparsity–entropy sweeps are shown in figures without numerical values in the text.

untested.parts: No measure of individual vision-model neurons responding to unrelated inputs. Raw-embedding entropy is over correlated pathology labels.
Superposition is assumed. The linearity check does not test whether features outnumber neurons or cause polysemanticity.
No change to the model's activation function, architecture or regularization. Only post-hoc SAEs are compared.
Not varied. The authors note only that naming is sensitive to the choice of top-activating samples.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked SAE-vs-raw rows to V1 and V5. However, an SAE is the study's own tool, not a change to the model, and the entropy measure over 14 co-occurring labels cannot establish unrelated-input polysemanticity. The raw-embedding entropy (2.38 of a maximum of about 3.81) gives at most weak, indirect evidence that raw dimensions are not label-selective. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Tests medical-image feature selectivity in MedCLIP embeddings, but not InceptionV1, the cited neuron, or whether multiple responses are to unrelated inputs.
No transformer language models, MLP neurons, tokens, or language contexts.
Tests linear reconstruction of composite-image embeddings, but not whether the number of features exceeds neuron capacity or whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity.
Does not test polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
Tests SAE features against raw MedCLIP embeddings and reports sparsity–entropy trends, but not alternative activation functions, modern convnets, or downstream task performance costs.
Does not revisit canonical polysemantic neurons or test whether apparently unrelated inputs share a feature such as pose.
Uses correlation entropy and interpretation detection, and notes sensitivity to selected activating samples, but does not systematically vary activation range or explanation-scoring method.

rows.subject: MedCLIP-ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared average neuron-class correlation entropy for SAE features and raw embeddings.

conditions.value: selected MedSAE versus raw MedCLIP embeddings

rows.measure: Average correlation entropy across neurons; lower entropy indicates more concentrated class associations.
rows.note: The paper reports these as the raw-embedding and SAE entropy values. This is a measure of class-association concentration, not a direct test of unrelated input mixtures.
rows.check: Compares the study's own SAE features with raw embedding dimensions (2.25 vs 2.38). This is method performance, not a polysemanticity rate of model neurons. Entropy over co-occurring pathology labels cannot show 'unrelated' mixtures. Unlink from V1 and V5.

rows.subject: MedCLIP-ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Measured interpretation-detection accuracy for SAE features.

conditions.value: 30 activating and 30 random non-activating images; activating samples defined by activation greater than 1 × 10−7

rows.measure: Count of neuron interpretations with detection accuracy above 70%.
rows.note: Aggregate counts stated by the authors; Table 2 lists the 21 SAE features individually. It does not report a polysemantic-neuron rate.
rows.check: Counts of interpretations above 70% detection accuracy: 21 for SAE, 2 for raw. This measures the SAE method's performance. The raw denominator is not stated, so no polysemantic share can be read. Unlink from V1 and V5.

rows.subject: MedCLIP-ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Selected a model by neuron-class entropy and reported its sparsity and reconstruction metrics.
rows.measure: L0 activation rate, fraction of variance explained, and dead neurons.
rows.value: 0.20% L0 activation rate; 0.98 fraction of variance explained; 30% dead neurons
rows.note: These figures describe sparsity and reconstruction, not downstream model performance or the rate of polysemantic neurons.
rows.check: Values for the SAE configuration chosen by best entropy (L0 0.20%, FVE 0.98, 30% dead). These are selection and configuration values and should not be a result row.

rows.subject: MedCLIP-ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed how sparsity–reconstruction trade-offs relate to mean top-class correlation.
rows.measure: Mean top-class correlation.
rows.value: Figure only; text says better reconstruction performance tends to coincide with higher mean top-class correlation.
rows.note: No sweep values are stated in the text.
rows.check: SAE hyperparameter-sweep trend, figure only. It concerns SAE training, not the model's architecture or training.

rows.subject: MedCLIP-ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed entropy across sparsity–reconstruction trade-offs.
rows.measure: Mean entropy of top-correlated neurons.
rows.value: Figure only; text says lower entropy is generally associated with better trade-offs, but entropy begins to increase past a certain sparsity level (low L0).
rows.note: The relationship is stated to be non-monotonic; no particular threshold or sweep values are given in the text.
rows.check: Non-monotonic entropy across SAE sparsity settings. This is a property of the SAE tool, not of the model's neurons. Unlink from V5.

rows.subject: MedCLIP-ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Embedded composite images and fit scalar weights to reconstruct their embeddings from the two component-image embeddings.

conditions.value: 100,000 randomly sampled image pairs from the 200k CheXpert training set
two images placed in opposing quadrants of a blank canvas

rows.measure: Fitted component weights and cosine similarity between predicted and actual composite embeddings.
rows.note: The authors say the high cosine similarity supports linear superposition in MedCLIP’s embedding space; this does not test capacity pressure as a cause of polysemanticity.
rows.check: The link is correct: this is an embedding-linearity sanity check (cosine 0.97) and does not test capacity pressure as a cause of polysemanticity.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MedSAE features compared with raw MedCLIP embeddings on CheXpert
reader_labels.reason: SAE features have lower average class-correlation entropy (r1), and the paper reports 21 SAE interpretations above 70% detection accuracy versus two for raw embeddings (r2); individual SAE interpretations are listed in r3–r23.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that the entropy relationship is not monotonic and that entropy rises beyond a certain sparsity level (r29); they also report only one MedCLIP-ResNet backbone.
